english.title: Owner of ship proceeding / attempting to proceed on a voyage / excursion without carrying on board an approved plan

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Merchant Shipping Safety of Navigation Regulations 2002

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the owner of **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), a ship to which regulation 7(3) of Chapter V of the Annex to the SOLAS convention applied and which

(A)_[proceeded]_
(B)_[attempted to proceed]_

on a voyage or excursion without complying with the requirement to carry on board a plan approved in accordance with paragraph 2 of Schedule 3 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 2 of Schedule 4 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Paragraph 2 of Schedule 4 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation)Regulations 2002 provides that it will be the owner of the ship who will be guilty of this offence.
(ii) Paragraph 22 of Schedule 4 to the MerchantShipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002 provides that it shall be a defence for a person charged under theseRegulations to show that he took all reasonable steps to avoid the commissionof the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
